item.title: Watch Live: Lindsay Clancy's psychiatrists begin testifying at her trial
item.description: Psychiatrists who treated Lindsay Clancy​ before she killed her children in Massachusetts began testifying at her trial Friday.

item.title: How long will a creditor try to collect on credit card debt before giving up?
item.description: You may think creditors will eventually stop trying to collect on unpaid debt, but the reality is more complicated.

item.title: July jobs report reveals unexpected loss of 23,000 jobs
item.description: Friday's jobs report showed employers shed jobs last month, rather than adding 95,000 new hires that had been forecast by economists.

item.title: Lisa Murkowski says she will oppose Todd Blanche's attorney general nomination
item.description: Alaska Republican Sen. Lisa Murkowski announced that she will oppose Todd Blanche's attorney general nomination. CBS News' Nikole Killion reports.

item.title: Trump's firings of federal officials set stage for next presidential power test
item.description: A federal appeals court is set to consider President Trump's effort to fire two immigration judges this fall, a case that could have significant implications for federal workers.

item.title: How Trump is targeting birthright citizenship again despite the Supreme Court halting his first bid
item.description: President Trump is trying again to curb birthright citizenship with executive action, despite a Supreme Court ruling blocking his first attempt. CBS News' Weijia Jiang reports.

item.title: "Ted Lasso" actors Juno Temple and Hannah Waddingham talk season 4
item.description: Emmy Award-winning actors Juno Temple and Hannah Waddingham share their thoughts on returning to "Ted Lasso" for a fourth season after a three-year hiatus. Temple returns as publicist Keeley Jones while Waddingham is back as club owner Rebecca Welton.

item.title: These NYC centers allow hard drug use in-house. Nearly 5 years in, is it helping?
item.description: An addiction-services nonprofit approved by the city focuses on harm reduction for hard drug users — to the chagrin of some in the neighborhood.

item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (Aug. 9)
item.description: A look at the features for this week's broadcast of the Emmy-winning program, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.title: Inside the NYC supervised drug-use sites focusing on harm reduction
item.description: A 5-year-old experiment sanctioned by the city of New York, but not by the federal government, provide supervised sites for drug users. The goal is to reduce overdose deaths and street drug use, but some critics still have doubts about the process. CBS News' Anna Schecter reports.

item.title: Organ nonprofit Network For Hope shut down over allegations some donors may have been alive
item.description: Health and Human Services has decertified Network For Hope, a Kentucky-based organ procurement group, after allegations they did not follow proper safety procedures. Would-be donor TJ Hoover was hospitalized after a cardiac arrest. His family says that despite medical staff documenting improved neurological function, organ donor evaluation continued. Hoover survived. Network For Hope says they will appeal the decision.

item.title: Amanda Knox defends comedy show amid sensitivity criticisms
item.description: Amanda Knox is known for being convicted, then acquitted, of the murder of her former housemate, British student Meredith Kercher. Today, she begins a run as a stand-up comic. However, Kercher's family is criticizing Knox's show as insensitive.

item.title: Yemen's Houthis escalate deadly attacks on Saudi-backed troops
item.description: Yemen's Houthi rebels launch fresh attacks on Saudi-backed government troops, says Yemeni state media, as Cruz says Trump must seek "regime collapse."

item.title: Don Lemon seeks dismissal of criminal charges, claims vindictive prosecution
item.description: Former CNN anchor Don Lemon's attorneys wrote that Trump's animosity toward Lemon "is well documented, stretching back over a decade."

item.title: Rand Paul asks Justice Department to charge Fauci after contempt vote
item.description: Republican Sen. Rand Paul asked the Department of Justice to charge Dr. Anthony Fauci with contempt of Congress after Fauci pleaded the Fifth during a hearing on the origins of the COVID-19 pandemic.

item.title: Florida man allegedly cut off teen lobster diver's air supply during fight
item.description: Former Florida boating safety task force member Michael Simpson was charged with attempted second-degree murder after allegedly cutting off a teen diver's air supply during a confrontation over lobster hunting.

item.title: Americans got their biggest raises in 40 years. Inflation took most of it.
item.description: The typical American's paycheck has grown faster since 2019 than in any stretch since the early 1980s. But prices climbed nearly as fast, swallowing about 80% of the wage increase.

item.title: Will Iran and Oman jointly control traffic in the Strait of Hormuz?
item.description: Iran said it is close to finalizing a deal with Oman to jointly control the Strait of Hormuz, but Iran added that it does not mean the strait will be fully open and it could include a toll. Charlie D'Agata has context.

item.title: Experts urge parents exercise caution over popular squishy toys
item.description: Squishy toys are all the rage on social media, from popular NeeDohs to other fun fidgets, but parents should be cautious of potential safety issues, as counterfeits may contain hazardous chemicals and attempts to heat or microwave the toys could lead to a dangerous explosion.

item.title: Meta fined $567 million over child safety issues
item.description: Meta, the tech giant that operates Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and other platforms, faces another financial penalty for allegedly failing to keep kids safe. A New Mexico judge has ordered Meta to pay $567 million for its failure to warn the public about the dangers its products pose to children.

item.title: Airlines push back against rising ICE arrests at airports
item.description: Immigration and Customs Enforcement arrests at airports have risen. Airlines are saying the arrests could put employees and passengers at risk and are hoping for changes.

item.title: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan sign key defense agreement, officials say
item.description: The agreement says any armed attack against one of the three states will be regarded as an attack on them all, Pakistan and Turkey said in statement.

item.title: Trump tries to restrict birthright citizenship again with new executive orders
item.description: In another attempt to target birthright citizenship, President Trump signed two executive orders to limit who is eligible for birthright citizenship. The Supreme Court struck down Mr. Trump's first move to completely end birthright citizenship.

item.title: Puerto Rico's ongoing water crisis leads to rationing
item.description: Puerto Rico's water crisis is worsening amid an ongoing drought and aging infrastructure. Residents in some communities have been without reliable water for over 100 days. Now, over 180,000 households will be without water for 48 hours at a time as government rationing begins.

item.title: Puerto Rico faces harsh water rationing measures
item.description: Some Puerto Ricans are waking up to no running water as the island faces harsh water rationing measures due to a drought. CBS News' Lilia Luciano reports.

item.title: Airlines blast mounting ICE arrests at airports
item.description: Airlines are decrying immigration arrests at airports as the Trump administration's detentions continue to grow. CBS News' Kris Van Cleave reports.

item.title: Feds could scrap rules requiring airlines to disclose airfares in full
item.description: A Transportation Department proposal could obscure the cost of a plane ticket, aviation experts warn. Here's what to know.

item.title: Cruz calls for arming Iran's protesters: "Our objective should be regime collapse"
item.description: GOP Sen. Ted Cruz told Aaron MacLean on the "School of War" podcast that President Trump should heap more pressure on Iran — including by arming Iranians to "let them overthrow their own government."

item.title: Trump-endorsed Rep. Andy Ogles projected to lose GOP primary in Tennessee
item.description: Two-term Rep. Andy Ogles lost the Republican primary for his Tennessee House seat, the Associated Press projects, despite securing an endorsement from President Trump.

item.title: Sen. Marsha Blackburn wins Republican primary for Tennessee governor
item.description: Sen. Marsha Blackburn had faced two primary challengers, including Rep. John Rose.
